Direct 45 degree leg press EMG study in 14 women comparing 45 degree, high-foot, and low-foot conditions at 40% and 80% 1RM. Measured rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, biceps femoris, gastrocnemius, and gluteus maximus.
Direct inclined leg press study on foot position and execution velocity effects. Used for foot-placement/velocity limitations and primary/secondary role support.
Direct leg press quadriceps EMG technique study. Used for quadriceps primary role and technique sensitivity.
Direct leg press versus single-joint exercise EMG in trained men, measuring quadriceps heads, gluteus maximus, and biceps femoris. Used for primary and secondary roles.
Direct squat and high/low foot leg press biomechanics/EMG source with stance and foot-angle variations. Used for hamstrings, gastrocnemius, knee-loading interpretation, and limitations.
Eight-week parallel squat versus 45 degree leg press training study in students. Used for athletic transfer and machine-specific strength interpretation.
